pl-l3d40c3-d1e115.summary: Distinguishes the letter of the Gospel from that of the Law: their promises differ, the Law promising earthly things and the Gospel heavenly; their sacraments differ, the Law's only signifying, the Gospel's conferring grace; their ceremonial precepts differ, while the moral ones are the same but more fully contained in the Gospel.
claims: The Law promises earthly goods, the Gospel heavenly.
The Gospel's sacraments confer grace; the Law's only signify.
Moral precepts are the same in Law and Gospel.

pl-l3d40c3-d1e118.summary: Concludes the book: you have heard the ten strings of the psaltery, given to both sexes, to be plucked with charity so that the beasts of the vices may be slain.
claims: The ten commandments are fulfilled through charity.

pl-l3d40c3.summary: Distinguishes the letter of the Gospel from that of the Law: the Law promises earthly things, the Gospel heavenly; the Law's sacraments only signify, the Gospel's confer grace; the ceremonial precepts differ, while the moral ones are the same but more fully contained in the Gospel. Book 3 closes with the image of the ten strings of the psaltery, given to both sexes, to be plucked by charity so that the beasts of the vices may be slain.
claims: The Law promises earthly things, the Gospel heavenly ones.
The Law's sacraments only signify, the Gospel's confer grace.
The moral precepts of the Law and Gospel are the same, but fuller in the Gospel.
The ten commandments are fulfilled by charity.
